utterances.text: Item 191 is Hazim Mujanovic, born in 1980, and so on. Mr. Cekic, there were a number of children detained at Batkovic during your time there. Did you -- didn't you see them there?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO CEKIC
utterances.text: Yes. All those persons, just like the previous one who was born in 1924, they were all brought with those who were captured during the breakthrough on the front line. That means that they either fought or joined the combatants. The Army of Republika Srpska, when they captured them, they couldn't be the judge of --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. Cekic, I only asked for whether you knew that children were there, and we just saw there were children. So we can move on. You told us in paragraph 19 about Vanekov Mlin. This prison was located in an old building nearby the Bijeljina garrison, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO CEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Srebrenica prisoners were held there including Sado Ramic whose statement you have commented, Mr. Cekic. Did you also know that Avdo Palic from Zepa was held also at Mlin? Did you know that, Mr. Cekic?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO CEKIC
utterances.text: No. I had no information about the Vanekov Mlin because those people were all under investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Thank you and that's statement. This Chamber has received evidence that Avdo Palic was brought to Mlin from Rogatica around 10 August, 1995, in order to be hidden from the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: This is at transcript page 3446465 and Exhibit P06156, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Sado Ramic, Mr. Cekic, whose statement you have commented, said that Avdo Palic was brought to Mlin during his detection there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 24779.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: And this is receipt on hand over of Avdo Palic to Dragomir Pecanac on 5 September, 1995, for the needs of the VRS Main Staff intelligence sector? According to the heading of the document, the prison Mlin was under the head of Bijeljina garrison, and Milan Savic was in charge of the prison. Is this correct, Mr. Cekic?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO CEKIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. All that has been noted is that the head of the prison is Milan Savic. There's nothing about the content of the document that has been confirmed by this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: This whole topic I'm talking about Avdo Palic and his imprisonment at Mlin. So this is another confirmation that this person was held there. The witness had said that he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But at least you could have asked if this is signed by Milan Savic to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: I'll do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. Cekic, if you look the signatures and the one that's on the middle, that's -- do you recognise as the signature of Milan Savic?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO CEKIC
utterances.text: No. I can't recognise the signature because I was not his superior. I've not seen his signature before. I'm in no position to say whether he signed this or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness confirmed that the prison was under the Bijeljina garrison and that Milan Savic was head of the prison so on that basis this document can be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Zec, until the time we are satisfied about the provenance or the other foundation, we'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI P6262, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I see the time. The only I have is three photographs of Batkovic to show to the witness with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Zec.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 24881.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: And, Mr. Cekic, what I would like to show you now is photographs of Batkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure, did you tender or did you not 24883?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: I believe that was his statement, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ah, yes. That was the statement. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. Cekic, if you look at the photo in front of you, in 1995 the prisoners were held in the first hangar looking from the top, the one near the small house with red roof; correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO CEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Can we have next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: This is the entrance to Batkovic, is it?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO CEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Can we have next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: And here we see these open hangars of the Batkovic complex, Mr. Cekic; correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO CEKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. President, these photos are from June 2009, and I tender these photos.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll receive them.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6263, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: I have nothing further. Thank you very much. Thank you very much, Mr. Cekic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have re-examination, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do, your Excellency, yes. May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Help us, Mr. Cekic, and shed light on some things. You started saying something about the military which captured those combatants, including a few who were younger. Can you finish that answer of yours?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO CEKIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the indictment, I saw that there was a number of persons in Batkovic aged between 15 and 18 and a number of those who were over 70. Both groups were brought together with those people who were combatants and who were taken as prisoners of war. However, those who imprisoned them, the VRS army, that is, could not separate them from each other. They couldn't know who were combatants irrespective of their age. That's why they were all brought together. A few days later or perhaps a fortnight or 20 days later, we separated a group of some 50 or 60 elderly people. We did not even exchange them because we were absolutely certain that they could no -- not be engaged in the BiH Army in the future. And we released them. We did not even need to exchange them. We allowed them to go to the territory of the federation, i.e., they went to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid that the transcript did not understand you. I don't want to be accused of anything, especially not of a leading question. Are you saying that you released them unilaterally without any compensation?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO CEKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we released them unilaterally. We did not ask for any of our own prisoners in return for those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Several questions were put to you by Mr. Zec on pages from 77 through 80. You said, "I didn't know." When he asked you if you knew, you said, "I didn't know." Did you subsequently learn that the abuses were going on before you became commander? When did you learn about possible abuses before you took over?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO CEKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I understand your question. I did for the legal representative about any abuses, I did not have any suspicions that there was such abuses, because what I heard here is something that my guards would not do, something that is very hard for me to believe. I learned something else from those people who had arrived there Srebrenica. When they got off the lorries and when they were lined up and when we took them to the hangar, the doctor came, the International Committee of the Red Cross came. We sent somebody to fetch food. They were fed. And then one of them stood up, I don't know his name, I never asked him, and he said, "You see how they lied to us? Our superior lied to us that when we arrived here in the prison in Batkovic there would be two men waiting for us with batons who would beat us up, that we would not be given any food, that we would be beaten up and ill-treated and so on and so forth. And we were also told that we would be better off dead, killed in combat than ending up in the Batkovici collection centre."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now can you tell us, you were asked on page 80 whether the prison?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. If I can intervene. Mr. Cekic, a moment ago you said in the indictment you saw that there was a number of persons in Batkovic aged between 15 and 18 and a number of those who were over 70. What indictment did you refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, the -- your sentence -- in your sentence there are two different words used for the indictment. The first part of your sentence was translated as judgement, and the second part as indictment. Can we do something about the interpretation? Can it be more accurate? On the record we see the word "indictment," and your words were interpreted as if you said "judgement." If somebody were to listen to the tapes, you would see that I'm right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But having heard -- having heard Mr. Karadzic's explanation, do you understand my question? Do you remember having said that, Mr. Cekic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what we're talking about here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. When Mr. Karadzic started his re-examination, you were asked -- he asked you to complete the answer you were stopped in one way or another, and then you said: "Yes." This is quote from your answer: "Yes. In the indictment I saw that there were a number of persons in Batkovic aged between 15 and 18 and a number of those who were over 70." And you further explained both groups were brought together with people who were combatants. Do you remember now having said that, Mr. Cekic? My question was what indictment you referred to? What indictment did you read?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, I don't understand, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. I'll leave it at that. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cekic, did you mention any indictments at all?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO CEKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The problem is in the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter notes that the witness did mention the word "optuznica" which stands for "indictment" in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the position on page 80 when you were asked about the competence of the command of the East Bosnia Corps? What was the position of the command of the East Bosnia Corps with regard to honouring the rights of prisoners of war and their treatment in Batkovic?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO CEKIC
utterances.text: The position of the command of the East Bosnia Corps was that the prisoners of war in Batkovic should not undergo any coercion or -- or punishment. Only the measures that are provided for in the Geneva Conventions could be applied, and we adhered to that. The person who drew my attention to that was the commander of the East Bosnia Corps when I took over duties in Batkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A document was shown to you, and in it you can see that 16 prisoners were taken to work.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up 65 ter 14871.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please pay attention to the fact that on the 25th of March, 1995, the command of the East Bosnia Corps issued this order. I'm looking for page 5. The same page in English, please. Now I'm going to read this. Page 5 in English. Before 73 -- at the end of 7.2. In English it's after brief interviews. It says here: "The prisoners of war are to be escorted to the Batkovic collection centre for further treatment and processing. Prevent any abuse of the prisoners of war with a view to their possible exchange for our captured soldiers." Were you familiar with the position of the commander of the East Bosnia Corps?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO CEKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of that position.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3240, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cekic, did you have any impression or knowledge as to my position vis-a-vis respecting international humanitarian law or did you see any order of mine to that effect?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO CEKIC
utterances.text: No, I had no such occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: To see such an order?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO CEKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't see such an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But were you aware of my position through someone else?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO CEKIC
utterances.text: I did know of your position because twice I was present in the barracks when you held a meeting, and you said to everyone there what your position was, that the population should not be driven away, that everyone should be treated equally, and some people, some civilians were even accommodated in the barracks. So I was completely familiar with your position in that regard. It did not differ as compared to the position we just saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What nationality were the civilians accommodated or who took shelter in the barracks?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO CEKIC
utterances.text: There were Croats, Muslims, Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO CEKIC
utterances.text: The Roma.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. 65 ter document 24879. Perhaps we don't need it on the screen. It is the military post 7102, Bijeljina. It reads: "Pursuant to the order of the president of the Presidency of Republika Srpska number 01827/92 of the 8th of September, 1992 --" well, it actually discusses departure of 16 people to work on -- on the nearby river to help out with the boats.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In any case could we look at 1D7995, which is actually the reference to the number quoted therein. 1D7995. Your Excellencies, may we go up till 3.00 today or do we need to break for the day and continue tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We need to rise at least 5 to 3.00 or possibly 10 to 3.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, this document is -- can be seen in e-court by the Defence but not by anybody else, so I'm giving a hard copy to be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The date is the 8th of September, 1992. The number is -- can we go down a bit? [In English] Okay. [Interpretation] 10-827/922. Is this the document quoted in the previous one? We can all see that it is so. In any case, since there is no translation, Mr. Cekic, I wanted to introduce the gist of the document. It says "Strictly confidential, urgent. Telegram to all municipal presidents in the RS." And then it says: "In keeping with my order of the 13th of July 1992 on respecting international humanitarian law when treating prisoners of war, I remind you that you are personally responsible for events in the territory of your municipality. In that regard, I remind you that in the prisons and collection centres people should not be held against their will if they are civilian and if they did not commit any crime. You also -- you need to release them safely to the territory where they seek to go to take shelter from the war or the activities of the war." I'll move on to the last paragraph now. "You are also duty-bound to respect the Geneva Conventions when treating prisoners -- or, rather, in both treating the prisoners and their registration and reporting to our Red Cross, which is under an obligation to report; the Belgrade mission of the ICRC in Ruzvelta Street 61. The prison guards must accommodate requests of the ICRC and the UNHCR." Since you read and speak Serbian, can you tell us whether this order says anything about work obligation?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO CEKIC
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This order of mine of the 8th of September, how does it fit with your knowledge as regards my position and the position conveyed to the military and civilian authorities?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO CEKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Those were your positions, and it fits completely into the position that was conveyed to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D3241, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the witness can return tomorrow, we'll need him for another 20 minutes. It's better to do that than to rush things today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Unless it causes a lot of problem with you, Mr. Cekic, we'll adjourn for today.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it doesn't.
